sector: Independent all-day cafe and counter service, lunch sandwiches and bowls, small plates and wine after four, serving a neighbourhood in food and hospitality.
founded_place_size: Brooklyn, New York; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
about: Corner and Cure is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is Brooklyn, New York, and this commission covers phase 1: food image system and seasonal launch assets.
audience: Neighbourhood regulars aged 25 to 45 who come in twice a week, know the counter staff, and read the screens over the pass from across the room. Local, food-literate, loyal, and quick to distrust anything that reads as styled to death.
price_positioning: Mid-market all-day cafe. Mains 16 to 24 dollars, wine by the glass 11 to 15. Sits comfortably above fast-casual counters and well below the tasting-menu rooms downtown.
typography: Display in a warm humanist serif with a little ink to it, set large so a dish name reads across the counter. Text and prices in a plain, open sans that stays legible at small sizes. The feel is elevated but comfortable, closer to a chalkboard than a wine list.
voice: Plain, warm, never fussy. We talk about burnt butter, the good bread and scrubbed oak, and we let the food carry the sentence. Example line: 'Small plates and a glass of something, most nights until late.'
brand_assets_status: No brand kit survives. The printed table dish cards exist only as the flat file our printer sent to press last spring, and she has since retired, so there is no working layout and no editable source. The photographed dishes and the till copy Danny writes are the only current materials, and both are considered final.
values: Real portions, honest cooking, and copy that is never reworded or cut, because the allergen line matters.
